questions.question: When can two matrices written in the same block layout be added block by block?
options: Whenever the total number of scalar entries is the same.
Only when every block is square.
When corresponding blocks have matching sizes.
Only when all off-diagonal blocks are zero.

questions.question: Why does block notation sometimes let a large matrix calculation look smaller?
options: It lets compatible submatrices be treated like larger entries.
It turns every block into a scalar number.
It changes a non-square matrix into a square matrix.
It removes the need to check dimensions.

questions.question: Before multiplying two block matrices using a row-by-column block pattern, what must be checked?
options: The two matrices must have the same number of rows.
The inner block dimensions must be compatible.
The diagonal blocks must all be zero.

questions.question: Suppose a block row is written as $\begin{pmatrix}A&B\end{pmatrix}$, where $A$ is $2\times3$. What must be true about $B$?
For block matrices $\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}E&F\\G&H\end{pmatrix}$, what is the $(1,2)$ block of their product?
A $3\times5$ matrix is split after row $1$ and after column $2$. What is the size of the upper-right block?
Does writing a matrix in block form create a new matrix?
options: No, because block form is allowed only for diagonal matrices.
Yes, each block becomes an independent matrix unrelated to the original.
Yes, block form always changes the determinant.
No, it is the same matrix with a chosen partition.

questions.question: Why are submatrices the natural building pieces of block matrices?
options: Each block must be square, as in a block diagonal matrix.
Each block may list the original rows and columns in any order.
Each block is a submatrix: some rows and columns of the original.
Each block is a minor, that is, a determinant of part of the matrix.

questions.question: If $A$ is $2\times2$, $B$ is $2\times1$, $C$ is $1\times2$, and $D$ is $1\times1$, what is the size of $\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}$?

Let $\boldsymbol{A}=\begin{pmatrix}\boldsymbol{A}_{11}&\boldsymbol{A}_{12}\\\boldsymbol{A}_{21}&\boldsymbol{A}_{22}\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{B}=\begin{pmatrix}\boldsymbol{B}_{11}&\boldsymbol{B}_{12}\\\boldsymbol{B}_{21}&\boldsymbol{B}_{22}\end{pmatrix}$ be partitioned so that $\boldsymbol{B}\boldsymbol{A}$ can be computed blockwise. What is the top-left block of $\boldsymbol{B}\boldsymbol{A}$?
